instruction: Set VLC's maximum volume to 200% in its preferences.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened terminal, verified src.mp4 exists, used VLC CLI scene filter to extract 147 frames to /tmp/frame_extract/, then used ffmpeg to create GIF. The GIF was created but duration was ~14.7s instead of 5s, resulting in imperfect image comparison.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, run shell commands, use VLC command-line for frame extraction with scene filter, use ffmpeg for conversion, navigate GIMP menus
metadata.failure_analysis: Model extracted frames from entire video segment instead of just 3-8s range, resulting in GIF duration mismatch. Also bypassed GIMP and used ffmpeg directly.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests VLC settings modification, a simpler task that the model can accomplish via terminal or VLC preferences GUI since it demonstrated VLC interaction capability
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VLC max volume setting to 200%. Postconfig kills VLC to save settings. Getter reads vlcrc for qt-max-volume. Metric awards 0.5 for active setting, 1.0 for correct value.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads qt-max-volume from ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc, which is the correct VLC config key for maximum volume percentage
Getter properly distinguishes between commented (default) and uncommented (actively set) lines, enabling partial credit
Postconfig correctly kills VLC before reading config to ensure settings are flushed to disk
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly as rules dict (expected.get('expected_max_volume', 200)) per framework convention
Partial credit scheme is reasonable: 0.5 for active setting, 1.0 for correct value and active
Expected value of 200 matches the instruction requirement of 200% maximum volume
Single instruction requirement (set max volume to 200%) is fully covered by the evaluator
